notes.summary: Partial P02.1: over every complete nontrivially valued field, the specified Gauss boundary jump on a strict n-polydisc (n>=2) has local continuous sequential approximation iff the residue field is countable. Decreasing semipositive real-PL nets always exist; this is not a net obstruction or an all-functions classification.
notes.detailedSummary: The coefficient-field, algebraic-closedness and discrete-valuation assumptions of the supplied Laurent-field example are unnecessary. Monic lifts of irreducible residue polynomials detect every non-Gauss point. Their finite products give decreasing semipositive strict real-PL nets. Countable residue field gives an explicitly cofinal sequence without a countable dense field assumption. Uncountable residue field supplies cofinite families of lifted residue points in every Gauss neighborhood, excluding even nonmonotone continuous pointwise sequences. The function satisfies the full scalar-extension classical curve-test definition, and the failure point lies in the actual relative boundary. The criterion is exact only for this function.
notes.text:
This is a partial mathematical draft, not an independent correctness verdict. Let K be any complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field, k its residue field, a in K with 0<|a|<1, and c=-log|a|. Put D=M(K<T>) and X_n=M(K<T_1,...,T_n>) for n>=2. Let eta be the Gauss point, p the first-coordinate projection, and i:D->X_n the analytic section with the other coordinates zero. Define w=1_{eta}, u=w composed with p, and x=i(eta). These are actual good strict affinoid spaces, separated and of dimensions 1 and n. Claim: u is finite bounded upper semicontinuous and classical psh, x lies in the relative boundary, and u has local pointwise continuous sequential approximation near x iff k is countable. In the countable case a decreasing finite semipositive real-PL sequence works on all of X_n. A decreasing semipositive real-PL net works for every k.

Primary inputs and scope. Classical psh means Definition 4.1 of Gubler–Rabinoff, Classically psh and pluriharmonic functions on Berkovich spaces, arXiv:2506.13548v2, 17 September 2025: upper semicontinuity and subharmonic pullback along every analytic curve after every analytic field extension. Definition 3.4 permits identically negative-infinite functions; Section 4.1.3 reduces testing to smooth connected strict scalar curves. Proposition 4.2(2),(3) supplies analytic logarithms, finite maxima and nonnegative real combinations. Theorem 4.3 states that, over a complete nontrivially valued field, an already real-valued real-PL function on a good strictly analytic space is semipositive iff it is classical psh. No separatedness, pure-dimensionality or boundaryless assumption is added. Semipositivity is geometric residue/model nefness, as in Gubler–Jell–Rabinoff, Forms on Berkovich spaces based on harmonic tropicalizations, arXiv:2111.05741v3, Proposition 7.1 and Definition 7.2: nonnegative degrees on integral proper residue curves.

The immediate applied statements and proofs were read in authenticated primary texts. The proof of the classical/real-PL comparison uses the distinct March paper On semipositive piecewise linear functions in non-archimedean analytic geometry, arXiv:2503.05513v1. Its actual curve comparison and smooth-curve recognition are Proposition 5.1 and Corollary 5.4; the June paper cites earlier labels 3.1 and 3.5. The March proof uses residue degrees, local lifting of residue curves and proper-surjective semipositivity descent. Deeper published foundations—including Thuillier harmonic comparison and Poincare–Lelong, Wanner's PL/current comparison inside that proof, formal models, Temkin reductions and degree projection formulas—are imported and disclosed, not freshly proved recursively. No book theorem or historical PASS receipt is a premise.

Legal truncation lemma. For an analytic f on a good strict space and b in K*, H=log max(|b|,|f|) is finite integral PL and semipositive. On each strict affinoid neighborhood the strict Laurent domains |f|<=|b| and |f|>=|b| form a finite G-cover. Their expressions are log|b| and log|f|. On the latter f is a unit, with inverse furnished by adjoining b/f. The expressions agree on the intersection. The cut is an actual field value, so the construction respects strictness. Analytic log/max laws make H classical psh; the already-real-PL comparison gives residue-nef semipositivity. Positive real multiples and finite positive sums remain semipositive real-PL by common refinement and the cone/comparison argument. This does not assume closure under maxima of arbitrary real-PL functions, which can fail in the strict topology.

Decreasing-limit justification. An infimum of decreasing finite continuous classical psh functions is upper semicontinuous because its strict sublevels are unions of open strict sublevels. After any scalar extension and smooth connected strict curve test, write the finite subharmonic pullbacks as g_i and their infimum as g. If g is identically negative infinity, it is allowed. Otherwise let A be a strictly affinoid test domain and H harmonic with g<=H on its finite boundary. For epsilon>0 choose an index at each boundary point with g_i<H+epsilon. Directedness supplies one upper bound for these finitely many indices. Harmonic comparison gives g_i<=H+epsilon throughout A. Taking the infimum and then epsilon to zero proves the required subharmonic test, including negative-infinite values. This agrees with GR Proposition 4.2(4).

Detection lemma. Let R be the set of monic irreducibles q in k[T], and choose monic lifts Q_q in K^circ[T]. Every y different from eta has |Q_q(y)|<1 for some q. A nonzero Tate series has attained Gauss norm in |K*| because its coefficients tend to zero. Dividing by an attaining coefficient gives norm one and a nonzero polynomial reduction. Reduction of products proves multiplicativity of the Gauss norm. Every bounded multiplicative seminorm is bounded by that norm: apply its boundedness inequality to f^N and take Nth roots. Distinctness from eta therefore gives f with |f(y)|<||f||. Normalize and factor its reduction as dbar times a product of irreducibles. Lift dbar to a unit d and form the corresponding product R_f of the Q_q. Then ||f-R_f||<1, also for nondiscrete valuations: the difference coefficients have norms less than one and tend to zero, so their attained maximum is less than one. Hence |R_f(y)|<1. Since each factor has norm at most one and d has norm one, some factor has norm less than one. A nonzero constant reduction cannot occur here. No coefficient subfield or algebraic closure is needed.

Net construction. Direct Fin(R) times the positive integers by inclusion and integer order. Put P_F=product of Q_q for q in F, with P_empty=1, and
V_(F,m)=c^(-1) log max(1,|a^(-1)P_F^m|)=max(0,1+(m/c)log|P_F|).
At zeros the first formula is finite. The truncation lemma and positive scaling prove semipositive strict real-PL membership. The second formula is only a numerical identity. Every factor has norm at most one, so increasing either index decreases V. At eta each monic product has norm one and V=1. Away from eta, a detecting factor of norm r<1 bounds every later term containing it by max(0,1+(m/c)log r), eventually zero. If r=0 the value is zero immediately. Thus V decreases to w. Substituting T_1 produces one globally defined net on X_n decreasing to u. The decreasing-limit argument proves classical admissibility with every scalar curve test.

Boundary. The closed Gauss singleton attains every analytic norm and is therefore the Shilov boundary. GR-C Section 3.1(3) identifies it with the relative boundary of the affinoid curve D. The boundary composition rule of Section 2.11(4') is equality for X_n->D->M(K), since D's structural map is separated. It gives p^(-1)(eta) contained in the actual relative boundary of X_n, including x. The indicator formula also proves upper semicontinuity directly.

Countable case. If k is countable, k[T] and R are countable. R is infinite by the product-plus-one argument. Enumerate q_1,q_2,... and take F_j={q_1,...,q_j}, m_j=j. For every finite F and every m, sufficiently large j contain F and satisfy j>=m. This proves cofinality and hence decreasing convergence of the displayed sequence. No second-countability or countable dense subset of K is assumed for this particular function.

Uncountable case. Choose one lift b_alpha in K^circ of each alpha in k and the rigid point z_alpha with T=b_alpha. Every neighborhood of eta contains all but finitely many z_alpha: a normalized Tate series has nonzero polynomial reduction, and outside its finitely many residue roots its evaluation equals its Gauss norm. A basic neighborhood imposes conditions on finitely many evaluations. Suppose continuous h_j on an ordinary neighborhood W of x converge pointwise to u. Continuity supplies neighborhoods N_j of eta inside i^(-1)(W) with |h_j(i(y))-h_j(x)|<1/4. Their exceptional residue classes form a countable union of finite sets. Choose alpha outside it. All inequalities then hold at z_alpha, contradicting h_j(x)->1 and h_j(i(z_alpha))->0. The points are distinct by evaluating T-b_alpha. Monotonicity was not used.

The obstruction also passes to higher-dimensional good strict spaces admitting an analytic retract D->Y->D, by restriction through the section. The polydiscs provide actual examples. All constructed expressions agree on intersections of their strict domains because they are restrictions of one formula. Over any analytic extension the original formulas converge to the pulled-back indicator; they need not converge to the native upstairs Gauss indicator.

This criterion is exact only for this function. It is a relative-boundary sequence obstruction and admits explicit decreasing nets. Countable residue is not asserted sufficient for every classical psh input, and the original P02.1 characterization remains unresolved. Full proofs are in P02.1-paper.tex and P02.1-whole-proof.md, with source boundaries in whole-source-application-ledger.md. Rerun: python programs/reproduce.py. These remain unverified drafts.

notes.summary: Partial P02.1 positive sector: negative logarithmic series of bounded analytic functions on good strict spaces have explicit decreasing semipositive real-PL sequences, including negative-infinite and noninvariant poles. The series representation is an extra hypothesis; arbitrary classical psh germs are not covered.
notes.detailedSummary: For |f_i|<=1 and positive real lambda_i, with no summability assumption, u_j=sum_(i<=j) lambda_i log max(|a|^j,|f_i|) is finite semipositive strict real-PL. Lowering thresholds and adding a nonpositive term proves monotonicity. Two-sided infimum inequalities prove the exact pointwise limit, including negative infinity. The formulas commute with scalar and morphism pullback and agree on strict-domain overlaps on one fixed space. An explicit Q_p bidisc example has infinitely many polar lines and fails maximal-compact-torus invariance. This is a starting-function sector, not an all-functions geometric regime.
notes.text:
Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, and X any good strictly K-analytic space. Give analytic functions f_1,f_2,... on this one X, bounded in absolute value by one, and real lambda_i>0. Define u=sum_i lambda_i log|f_i| as the infimum of its nonpositive finite partial sums, with log 0=-infinity. This definition uses analytic input data, not an approximation class. No continuity, finiteness or summability is assumed. Claim: u is classical psh and the decreasing pointwise limit on all of X of
u_j=sum_(i=1)^j lambda_i log max(|a|^j,|f_i|),
where a is fixed with 0<|a|<1. Every u_j is finite semipositive real-PL. Identically negative-infinite targets are permitted. Zero coefficients can be discarded.

The complete strict truncation and classical decreasing-limit lemmas, with exact primary-source conditions, are proved in n1 and used here. Each truncation is integral PL, cut at an actual field value |a|^j; real coefficients are applied afterward. No arbitrary-real-max closure, all-domain lisse identification, current recognition or smooth/FS comparison is used. Semipositivity is geometric residue/model nefness.

Proof. Each u_j is finite, continuous, nonpositive and semipositive real-PL by common refinement of its finitely many truncation covers. Increasing j lowers every old truncation threshold and adds a nonpositive summand, so u_(j+1)<=u_j. Omitting a nonpositive tail and clipping terms upward gives u_j>=u. Write ell=inf_j u_j. For fixed N and j>=N,
u_j<=sum_(i<=N) lambda_i log max(|a|^j,|f_i|).
At each point the finite sum on the right decreases to sum_(i<=N) lambda_i log|f_i|, including negative infinity when a factor vanishes. Hence ell is at most every finite partial sum, and therefore ell<=u. The reverse inequality was already proved, so ell=u everywhere, including divergent and polar cases. The decreasing-limit proof in n1 verifies upper semicontinuity and every scalar curve test.

All local expressions are restrictions of the same global formula and agree term by term on overlaps. Under an analytic morphism from a good strict source or any analytic field extension, use the pulled-back analytic functions. Their evaluations and bounds are the downstairs ones. The same truncation proof gives finite semipositive real-PL functions, decreasing to the pulled-back series. This concerns the original analytic data, not arbitrary new functions over an extension. No net extraction occurs: the sequence is explicitly constructed from the given countable family.

If C is compact and u is finite continuous on C, the increasing open subsets defined by u_j-u<epsilon cover C. Compactness supplies one index covering C, proving uniform convergence without metrizability. Only pointwise convergence is claimed for discontinuous or extended-valued targets.

Concrete noninvariant example. Over Q_p take the strict bidisc, f_1=T_1-T_2, f_i=T_1-p^(i-1)T_2 for i>=2, and lambda_i=2^(-i). All factors have norm at most one on the whole domain. At the Gauss point u=0. At (1,1) the first factor vanishes, giving u=-infinity. At (1+p,1), the first factor has norm |p| and all later factors have norm one, giving u=(1/2)log|p|. Multiplication of the first coordinate by the unit 1+p changes these values, so u is not invariant under the maximal compact torus. The sequence covers all its polar lines and relative-boundary points on one actual bidisc.

This is an explicit sufficient starting-function sector on good strict spaces. It does not prove that arbitrary classical psh functions have such a series representation, and therefore does not solve the original all-functions characterization. No FS, weakly smooth or ordinary CLD-smooth conclusion is inferred. Full proof: P02.1-whole-proof.md and standalone P02.1-paper.tex. Rerun: python programs/reproduce.py. This is an unverified draft relying on earlier own note n1, not supplied historical notes.

notes.summary: Scalar-extension distinction and deliverables: an explicit Gauss-valued extension of Q_p changes the native boundary-jump sequence criterion while preserving approximation of the pulled-back original function. The standalone paper, full proofs, scope/source ledgers and bounded checks are delivered. Full P02.1 remains unresolved; candidate=false.
notes.detailedSummary: Complete Q_p(t_alpha) for uncountably many independent variables with its Gauss valuation. Its residue field is the uncountable field F_p(t_alpha). By n1, the Q_p-native jump and its pullback have decreasing PL sequences, whereas the new native jump has no continuous sequence. Evaluation at T=t_alpha proves that these upstairs functions differ. All 46 manifest-bound files match their lengths and hashes, four fresh primary PDF extractions match their retained text, and bounded rational diagnostics pass. The standalone eight-page manuscript compiles successfully. These observations do not certify mathematics. Unused whole-book reading and recursive verification of deeper foundations are not claimed. The original geometric characterization remains unresolved.
notes.text:
For an analytic extension L/K, the n1 formulas formed with the original K-defined polynomials converge to w_K composed with the scalar projection pi:D_L->D_K. This follows from literal equality of analytic evaluations. Their support is pi^(-1)(eta_K), not necessarily the singleton eta_L. The n2 sequence likewise preserves approximation of the original analytic data. Neither statement concerns every new classical psh function over L.

Explicit field construction. Take K=Q_p, an uncountable index set A, and F=Q_p(t_alpha:alpha in A). Give each polynomial its Gauss norm, the maximum coefficient norm, and extend to fractions. Scalar normalization and multiplication of nonzero reductions in the domain F_p[t_alpha] prove multiplicativity. Each polynomial uses finitely many variables. The residue field is F_p(t_alpha:alpha in A): a unit fraction has equal numerator and denominator valuations, so cancelling their common scalar computes its residue as a quotient of nonzero reductions; every residue fraction lifts. Positive-valuation elements reduce to zero. Let L be the completion. Its residue field is unchanged because every integral element is within distance less than one of an element of F and has the same residue. Thus L is complete and nontrivially valued with uncountable residue field, while Q_p has finite residue field.

By n1, w_K has a decreasing semipositive real-PL sequence and its pullback retains that sequence on D_L. The native jump w_L=1_{eta_L} has no continuous pointwise sequence near eta_L. These functions actually differ. For a fixed alpha, the L-point T=t_alpha maps to eta_K: normalize any nonzero K-Tate series to norm one; its reduction is a nonzero polynomial in F_p[T], which evaluates nontrivially at the transcendental residue of t_alpha. Its value is therefore its Gauss norm. Equality for every analytic evaluation identifies its image as eta_K. Hence (w_K composed with pi)(t_alpha)=1, while w_L(t_alpha)=0. Substitution of T_1 gives the same distinction on higher-dimensional strict polydiscs. No full all-functions P02.1 property over Q_p is asserted.

Deliverables. P02.1-paper.tex is standalone and embeds all new proofs in an eight-page manuscript. P02.1-whole-proof.md is the full companion. whole-source-application-ledger.md records exact primary titles, versions, applied statements and proofs, hypotheses, the March/June numbering mismatch and deeper imported foundations. exact-scope.md, whole-proof-coverage.md, original-scope-noncircularity.md and acceptance-decision.json record the partial-only decision. Separate full note bodies are in notes/n1.md, notes/n2.md and notes/n3.md; actualFINAL.json records the delivery with candidate=false. Artifact filenames are evidence locations, not supports.

Execution observations. All 46 manifest-bound files matched their lengths and SHA-256 values. Whole sources were retained under LOCALONLY without executing supplied programs. Four primary PDFs—classical GR v2, PL GR v1, GJR v3 and Wu local v1—were freshly extracted with pdftotext -layout; all four complete extractions were byte-identical to their retained text. This verifies pairing, not correctness or whole physical reading. Public arXiv records independently authenticated titles, authors, versions and dates. Direct shell HTTP retrieval was denied; public web-tool metadata access succeeded without changing network settings.

The exact-rational program programs/check_formulas.py exhausts 125 three-term input tuples over {negative infinity,0,-1/3,-1,-4}, with weights (1/2,2/3,3/5), at six stages. It checks monotonicity, nonpositivity and the finite target lower bound. Its four-factor net proxy contains all 16 subsets at six stages: 96 indices and 1701 ordered comparable pairs. Every assertion passes. These are exhaustive finite results only for those specified proxies; they do not verify analytic geometry, uncountability, residue nefness or universal scalar curve tests.

Rerun from this directory with python programs/reproduce.py. Commands and complete outputs are saved in evidence/. Pandoc and both pdfLaTeX passes returned zero. The final PDF has eight pages and 311018 bytes; its final log has no box or warning diagnostics. The environment is Python 3.12.14, Pandoc 3.1.11.1, pdfTeX 3.141592653-2.6-1.40.26 with TeX Live 2025/dev/Debian, and pdftotext 25.03.0. The manuscript TeX SHA-256 is 9e40baaa81c9326382668d0c59dedaf7a1f8cee252610033d54ad7eb3c692bbd; the PDF SHA-256 is 7c6eb4cc66d5a7ac003d8f31d1a097130fafdfecb6e8daf3588b1a352fa2888c. Compilation and finite arithmetic are not mathematical certificates. No heavy computation, agents, extra model jobs, publication, catalogue action or editor changes were used.

Source and acceptance limitations. Historical mathematical bodies were reconstructed as data, preserving the restrictions on entire projective fibres, sequence-versus-net obstructions, and weak versus ordinary smoothness. No historical result or PASS receipt is a correctness premise. Complete immediate applied primary statements and proofs were read. Deeper recursive foundations are imported and disclosed; unused whole book chapters and unused private primary articles were retained and hashed but not freshly read in their entirety. No whole-paper correctness verdict is claimed for the September 2026 Wu preprint. Its Definition 3.8 defines an approximation-generated local class on projective analytifications; that definition alone does not provide the missing bridge for every extended classical curve-test input.

The original P02.1 target remains unresolved by this work. n1 gives an actual boundary sequence failure and a sharp threshold for one jump, while explicit nets still approximate it. n2 gives a noninvariant extended-pole sector with an extra analytic-series hypothesis. No noncircular classification for every arbitrary classical psh germ, boundaryless higher-dimensional classification, general normalization descent or arbitrary-chart extraction/gluing theorem is established. The implementation deliverable is complete as partial research; candidate=false and no original atom is counted solved. These proofs remain unverified drafts awaiting independent mathematical assessment.
